scenario: [LEXP.3.2] abs(x) over [LEXP.7.13.1]'s wrap: |INT64_MIN| = 2^63 has no Int representation, and the Int wrap makes it INT64_MIN, as unary `-` on INT64_MIN is (LEXP.7.13.1.neg_int64_min). The guard `abs(t.x) == t.x and t.x < 0` holds for exactly one Int, INT64_MIN. Path: builtins.c builtin_abs, which computed `v < 0 ? -v : v` in int64_t -- undefined behaviour at INT64_MIN, so an optimizer owed this answer nothing (audit finding I1) -- now int_ops.h ds_i64_abs over ds_i64_neg; Mercury ds.eval int64.abs. fact_count 2 = T plus the Hit the rule emits.
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    x: Int key

schema Hit scope logical:
    d: Int key

rule r:
    T t where abs(t.x) == t.x and t.x < 0
->
    emit Hit logical d: 0
